name: Geneva
tagline: A cosmopolitan lakeside city of diplomacy, watchmaking and parks, with the world's tallest fountain jet and Mont Blanc on the skyline.
highlight: The Jet d'Eau shooting 140 metres into the air, with the Alps and Mont Blanc behind on a clear day.
shortDescription: A French-speaking lakeside city, with the Jet d'Eau, the old town and St. Peter's Cathedral, the Reformation Wall, UN and Red Cross sites, watches and chocolate.
metaDescription: A Geneva travel guide: the Jet d'Eau, the old town and St. Peter's Cathedral, the Reformation Wall, Palais des Nations, Red Cross Museum, lake promenade, fondue, where to stay and a two-day plan.
knownFor: International diplomacy, Jet d'Eau, watches, lake
goodFor: City breaks, history, museums, lake walks, day trips to Mont Blanc

image.alt: The Jet d'Eau fountain rising from Lake Geneva

intro: Geneva sits at the south-western tip of Lake Geneva, where the Rhône flows out toward France, and it is surrounded by French territory on three sides. It is the second-largest city in Switzerland, home to about 200,000 people, and one of the most international, with the European headquarters of the United Nations, the Red Cross, the World Health Organization and dozens of other organisations.

The city's landmark is the Jet d'Eau, a fountain in the harbour that shoots water about 140 metres into the air, visible from across the city. On the left bank, the old town climbs a hill to St. Peter's Cathedral, where John Calvin preached, and the Reformation Wall in Parc des Bastions celebrates the leaders of the Protestant movement. Along the lakeshore, promenades, parks and swimming spots run for kilometres, and on clear days Mont Blanc floats on the horizon.

Geneva is also a city of museums, watches and chocolate, and a base for exploring Lake Geneva, the Jura and Chamonix, an hour away in France. It is expensive, but rewarding, and two days is enough for the main sights.

whyVisit.intro: Geneva is a polished, international city on one of Europe's great lakes.

points.title: International sites
points.text: The UN and the Red Cross.

points.title: Gateway
points.text: To the lake, Chamonix and the Alps.

attractionsIntro: The sights are compact, on both sides of the lake and river.

attractions.name: Jet d'Eau

image.alt: The Jet d'Eau in Geneva harbour

attractions.text: A fountain that shoots 500 litres of water per second to a height of about 140 metres, installed in 1891 and now the city's symbol.
attractions.tip: Walk out along the pier to feel the spray.

attractions.name: Lake Geneva promenade

image.file: File:Lake Geneva @ Promenade @ Quai du Mont Blanc @ Geneva (42465168860).jpg
image.alt: The Quai du Mont Blanc promenade on the shore of Lake Geneva

attractions.text: A lakeside walk from the Jet d'Eau to the Bains des Pâquis, with views to the Alps and swimming platforms.
attractions.tip: Swim at the Bains des Pâquis in summer.

attractions.name: St. Peter's Cathedral

image.alt: St. Peter's Cathedral rising above the old town of Geneva

attractions.text: The Protestant cathedral where John Calvin preached, with a tower climb for views and an archaeological site beneath.

attractions.name: Reformation Wall

image.alt: The Reformation Wall with large statues of Calvin, Farel, Beza and Knox

attractions.text: A 100-metre wall in Parc des Bastions with large statues of Calvin, Farel, Beza and Knox, and other reformers.
attractions.tip: Next to a giant chess set.

attractions.name: Palais des Nations
attractions.text: The UN's European headquarters, open for guided tours.

attractions.name: International Red Cross and Red Crescent Museum
attractions.text: A museum about humanitarian action and the movement founded in Geneva.

thingsToDoIntro: Geneva mixes lake time and museums.

thingsToDo.title: Swim at Bains des Pâquis
thingsToDo.text: A popular public bathing spot, with a sauna and fondue in winter.

thingsToDo.title: Take a lake cruise
thingsToDo.text: Boats run to Lausanne and Montreux.
thingsToDo.tip: Included in the Swiss Travel Pass.

thingsToDo.title: Take a day trip to Chamonix
thingsToDo.text: Visit Mont Blanc, an hour away in France.

thingsToDo.title: Visit the CERN
thingsToDo.text: The particle physics laboratory near the city.

foodIntro: Geneva's food mixes French and Swiss traditions.

accommodation.intro: Stay near the lake or the station.

gettingThere.intro: Geneva has an international airport and rail links.

options.text: About 7 to 10 minutes to Cornavin station.
options.detail: Free public transport ticket at the airport.

options.text: Under three hours from Zurich and about 1.5 hours from Bern.

gettingAround.intro: Trams, buses and boats cover the city.

options.detail: Hotel guests often get a free pass.

bestTime.headline: May–September
bestTime.summary: Geneva has warm summers and cool, grey winters.

itinerary.title: Two days in Geneva
itinerary.intro: The old town and the lake.

days.title: The old town
days.morning: St. Peter's Cathedral and the old town.
days.afternoon: The Reformation Wall and Parc des Bastions.

days.title: The lake
days.morning: Palais des Nations or the Red Cross Museum.
days.afternoon: Lake promenade and the Jet d'Eau.

tipsIntro: A few tips help you enjoy Geneva.
tips: Use the free transport ticket at the airport.
Ask your hotel for a transport pass.
Book UN tours ahead with your passport.
Swim in summer at the Bains des Pâquis.
Watch for the Jet d'Eau's schedule.
Bring a jacket for the wind.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Geneva?

faq.a: Yes, one of the most expensive cities.

faq.q: Is the Jet d'Eau always on?
faq.a: Usually, but it can stop in strong wind or frost.

faq.q: Is Geneva good for a day trip to Chamonix?
faq.a: Yes, about an hour by road or bus.
